summary:
Magallanes y Antártica Chilena falls under Chile's national framework, which is among the more developed in the region. Legal gender recognition rests on Gender Identity Law 21,120, in force since 27 December 2019: adults may change their registered name and sex on request to the Civil Registry without therapy or surgery. People aged 14 to 18 must apply to family courts with psychosocial and family-context antecedents, and the statute does not permit the procedure for those under 14 although it recognises them as transgender. On 9 April 2025 the Constitutional Court declared the 'over 14 years old' wording inapplicable as unconstitutional in a case brought by the mother of a 10-year-old trans girl, and that ruling applies only to that case.

The 2012 Zamudio Law prohibits discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, was extended to gender expression in 2018, and treats hate-crime motivation as an aggravating criminal circumstance. Same-sex marriage and joint adoption have been legal since March 2022, civil unions since 2015, and birth certificates offer a third sex option for intersex children.

Transphobic violence is documented nationally and in this region. The XXIII annual report of Movilh, published in March 2025 on 2024 data, places Magallanes at 0.96% of the national case total while recording it among the regions with the largest percentage increases, at +100% year-on-year. In Punta Arenas, trans woman Kenia Chacón was attacked in 2024 in a case prosecuted as attempted femicide; on 15 April 2026 SernamEG announced it would appeal the sentence, which imposed four years of partial internment against the five years of total internment the prosecution had sought, and the victim's mother publicly denounced that the attack was devalued because of her daughter's gender identity.

Nationally, a young trans man was murdered in 2023 in a killing covered up for 24 hours and described in national reporting as Chile's largest hate crime; the perpetrator, an acquaintance, confessed. In September 2021 a 20-year-old trans man and his girlfriend were beaten with bottles and clubs and held against their will for close to an hour at a Santiago hotel, where the attacker said he wanted to kill the victim.

Detention carries specific protections that reach this region. The national director of Gendarmería de Chile signed a protocol guaranteeing the gender identity of trans detainees, providing placement by assumed gender, segmented housing and rules on entry examinations, with a standing committee of Gendarmería and undersecretariat representatives overseeing implementation, including access rules for trans visitors.

Entry and removal rules reference gender identity. The Migration and Immigration Law of 11 April 2021 bans arbitrary discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity and offers protection to LGBT immigrants seeking asylum. Article 10 provides that recognised asylum seekers may be granted complementary protection, and no foreigner holding complementary protection may be expelled or returned to a country where their right to life, physical integrity or personal freedom is at risk on grounds including sexual orientation or gender identity.

Restrictive proposals are active but non-binding. On 15 May 2025 the Chamber of Deputies approved the CEI 57 commission report, 56 votes to 30 with 6 abstentions, a non-binding recommendation to eliminate the Gender Identity Support Program, restrict minors' progressive autonomy, ban hormonal treatment for minors and repeal the circular protecting gender identity in schools.
tangentialFactors:
Magallanes holds a small share of national case volume, 0.96% of the total recorded by Movilh for 2024, yet its year-on-year growth of +100% puts it among the regions where documented LGBTI incidents rose fastest. A low regional count therefore does not indicate a low or falling trend.

The Punta Arenas prosecution shows how sentencing can diverge from the charge in a gender-motivated case: attempted femicide was established, but the court imposed four years of partial internment where the prosecution sought five years of total internment, prompting an appeal by the national gender-equality service. The victim's mother framed the outcome as a devaluation of the attack based on her daughter's gender identity.

Violence against trans people in Chile has included lethal and near-lethal attacks with domestic or acquaintance settings rather than stranger encounters, as in the 2023 murder and the September 2021 hotel assault in Santiago, where the attacker stated an intent to kill.

The most restrictive legislative moves of 2025 operated through non-binding channels and a budget clause rather than a change to the Gender Identity Law itself. The CEI 57 report passed the Chamber of Deputies 56 to 30 with 6 abstentions but carries no legal force, while the Constitutional Court annulled the budget provision barring hormone financing for trans minors by seven votes to three on 9 January 2025.
localsOnly:
The public health system has funded sex reassignment surgery and hormone therapy since 2013, and a 2011 Ministry of Health circular obliges all care centres to register transgender patients by their social name.

Circular 7 of June 2024 suggested deferring the initiation of new gonadotropin-releasing hormone blockers and cross-sex hormone therapy in adolescents until national guidelines are published; the Medical College noted that physicians may still prescribe. On 9 January 2025 the Constitutional Court, by seven votes to three, annulled section 46 of the 2025 Budget Law, which had barred the Ministry of Health from financing hormone therapies for trans children and adolescents.

In November 2025 Congress defunded the Ministry of Social Development's Gender Identity Support Program through the 2026 Budget Law, but the Ministry of Health-run programme continues to provide support in medical centres. The Crece con Orgullo programme has operated since 2023 for children and adolescents aged 3 to 17.

Residents changing their registered name and sex follow the national procedure before the Civil Registry as adults, or before family courts between the ages of 14 and 18 with psychosocial and family-context antecedents.
outOfScopeNotes:
The outcome of SernamEG's announced appeal against the Kenia Chacón sentence is not sourced; the 15 April 2026 report establishes the intention to appeal, not any appellate decision.

No source in the inventory identifies which Gendarmería de Chile facility operates in Punta Arenas or how the national trans-detention protocol is applied at that site, so its practical availability to a detained visitor in this region remains unresolved.

Whether the national guidelines referenced in Circular 7 of June 2024 have since been published is not sourced here, leaving the position on initiating adolescent hormone therapy unresolved.

Nothing in the inventory addresses the availability of gender-affirming care providers, waiting times or social-name compliance in Magallanes facilities specifically.

The legislative fate of the CEI 57 recommendations beyond the Chamber of Deputies vote of 15 May 2025, including any Senate action or implementation, is not sourced.

No regional data appears in the inventory on the take-up of the third sex option on birth certificates or on any local anti-discrimination complaints brought under the Zamudio Law.
